speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when you first noticed these skin lesions and whether they have changed in size or appearance since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: The painless, nonpruritic nature of the lesions makes typical varicella unlikely, so I need to assess for other infectious causes. Are the papules firm and flesh-colored or pink, and do they appear to have a central dimple or umbilication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of pearly papules with central umbilication in a daycare setting is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
